claims.text: Optimizing additive-manufacturing temperature, pressure, and scanning speed will improve the dimensional precision of high-entropy-alloy components.
Optimizing additive-manufacturing temperature, pressure, and scanning speed will improve the mechanical integrity of high-entropy-alloy components.
Optimizing additive-manufacturing temperature, pressure, and scanning speed will reduce fabrication-induced defects.
The selected process parameters influence solidification during additive manufacturing.
Process-parameter optimization reduces porosity and other fabrication defects.
Process-parameter optimization promotes formation of a favorable microstructure.
Reduced defect density and a favorable microstructure improve mechanical properties.
The resulting microstructure and defect reduction improve dimensional precision.
Relative to standard processing, optimized processing will reduce deviation from nominal dimensions.
Relative to standard processing, optimized processing will increase tensile strength.
Relative to standard processing, optimized processing will increase toughness.
Relative to standard processing, optimized processing will increase fatigue resistance.
Relative to standard processing, optimized processing will decrease porosity and cracking.
The proposed effects are limited to additively manufactured high-entropy alloys and may not generalize to other alloy systems or manufacturing processes.
